rows.author: F100;
rows.title_short: Contra -  S O N A  Contra State Of The Nation Address
rows.abstract:
Rep. Colmenares took to task the five-year Aquino
Administration for invoking falsehoods and alleged
accomplishments under the Daang Matuwid program.
He enumerated one by one President Aquino´s promises to the Filipino people that were made in his yearly SONA beginning 2010 and that had never been realized and implemented, principal among which are the following: the end of lump-sum budgeting by instituting a zero-based budgeting in the National Budget; prosecution of perpetrators of human rights violations; cheaper source of energy; decline in criminality; massive
rehabilitation and recovery programs for the victims of various natural calamities; lessening of government subsidy to LRT and MRT; increase in daily and monthly wages for laborers and lowering of the poverty threshold. He maintained that the PNoy Administration´s claim to Daang Matuwid as a centerpiece poverty alleviation program of government had only led the most number of ordinary and poor Filipinos to the brink of poverty and hopelessness, with the more important programs for good governance intentionally
disregarded: the failure to enact into law a Freedom of Information Act; the institutionalization of pork barrel funds; the failure of the government to prosecute public
officials charged with graft and corruption; the failure to implement an equitable justice system to prevent harassment and unjust persecution; and the political vendetta that the Department of Justice has relentlessly pursued against the political opponents of the Aquino Administration.
He opined that President Aquino´s Daang Matuwid policy only led the country into unending poverty; paved the way straight to the precipice of
more serious difficulties; and directly led the country into the abyss of chronic corruption. He however expressed belief that corruption is not the root cause of poverty in the country but the absence of genuine land reform; lack of national industrialization; lack of fair distribution of property; absence of real independence and of true democracy. In closing, Rep. Colmenares presented the following recommendations to solve the country´s present ills: 1) passage of a genuine agrarian reform bill and provision of adequate support to farmers and the agricultural
sector; 2) introduction of reforms for national
industrialization; 3) increase of funding and public services for health, education, housing, irrigation, salary and pension; 4) increase in wages, lowering of the prices of commodities, and setting up of a progressive taxation system; 5) respect for human rights, release of political prisoners, and promotion of peace talks in the
country; 6) introduction of political and suffrage reforms to broaden the political participation of the poor majority; and 7) promotion and strengthening of national sovereignty and interest against the impositions of powerful countries like America and China.
INTERPELLATION OF MIN.LEADER ZAMORA (R.)
The two Members subsequently discussed the absurdity of a monthly poverty threshold of â‚±8,770 and the need for focus and funds for industrialization and employment generation rather than the palliative Conditional Cash Transfer (CCT) Program. Remarking that they should tackle valuable issues in the presence of more Members, Rep. Zamora said that he would also speak about the same at the proper time. INTERPELLATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ The Chair next recognized Rep. Jonathan A. Dela Cruz who asked about the performance of the PNoy Administration in social services. Rep. Colmenares criticized the privatization and deregulation of health
services and agreed with his colleague that the government promoted the interest of mass railway system concessionaires rather than the public.
Rep. Dela Cruz further raised the issue of the noninclusion in President Aquino´s SONA of the welfare of the overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) and their contributions to the national economy. Rep. Colmenares expressed agreement that the government has neglected the OFWs as the President vetoed the proposed Overseas Filipinos Legal Assistance Fund in 2014 thus ignoring the huge amount of remittances the OFWs had brought into the country. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.7,pp.26-27)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-08-10
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Zamora R. and Dela Cruz. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H073;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Paquiz dwelled on various issues confronting
the promotion and delivery of public health care services. Specifically, she discussed, among others, several concerns regarding food safety, primary health care, and the decreasing number of competent public health workers due to the rationalization plan of the government. She underscored that the legislators have the responsibility to ensure that the yearly expenditures for health, food safety, medicine procurement, health facility enhancements and human resource are utilized according to the mandate of the law. Refuting President Aquino´s statement in his recent SONA that massive PhilHealth benefits will assure the public of equitable access to health care services,
Rep. Paquiz emphasized that effective health
care for all can only be achieved by hiring the proper number of qualified public health workers. She then stressed the advocacy of Ang Nars Party-List for the full implementation of the Primary Health Care Program by allowing an equitable ratio between health facilities and workers. Finally, she asked that the appropriations for the Department of Health (DOH) be genuinely used for the implementation of more important health programs, allocation of salaries for permanent
positions, filling up of funded plantilla items, and increase in the salaries and benefits of health workers. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.7,p.27)

rows.author: H069;
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. Hicap expressed dismay
over the inaccurate presentation of the true conditions of the Filipino workers and farmers in the President´s recent SONA. Among others, he revealed how the PNoy Administration is guilty of violating the rights of the farmers, workers and the urban poor particularly in the following
matters: low wages and increasing prices of basic
goods and services; labor union-busting; failed implementation of the agrarian reform program which has wasted approximately P241 billion from July 1987 to December 2013 and has resulted in land grabbing problems; displacement of Lumads and farmers in Mindanao due to mining; dislocation of millions of farmers due to the Laguna Lake Dike Expressway projects and other land use conversion projects under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Program; workers´ lack of security of tenure, retrenchment, and plea for justice for the tragic death of Kentex workers. He then urged his colleagues to oppose the antiFilipino programs and policies for them to be able to really serve the Filipino masses. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.7,pp.29-30)

rows.author: H080;
rows.title_short: Stranded O F W S Bound For Libya
rows.abstract:
Rep. Señeres first acknowledged his guests who
were present in the gallery of the Session Hall.
He then spoke about the plight of 600 stranded
OFWs who used to work in multinationals and oil
companies in Libya but were repatriated in the Philippines by the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) due to perceived unstable security and political situation therein and in accordance with the revised Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act. He cited the huge losses and sacrifices made by them because of the adamance of the DFA to not downgrade the imposition of the mandatory repatriation or alert level 4 to voluntary repatriation or alert level 3 of OFWs in Libya. He likewise pointed out the lack of consideration
on the health and financial situations of these
workers and their families and also their lack of
knowledge on the exemption of the laws. In light thereof, Rep. Señeres moved to allow the immediate departure of these stranded OFWs so that they may be able to resume work and avail of their employment and or retirement benefits from their foreign employers. He also moved that his speech be referred immediately to the appropriate Committee for proper investigation in aid of legislation. 
(SOURCE: HOuse Journal No.7,p.30)

rows.author: H081;
rows.title_full: ON THE EVACUATION OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES (LUMADS) IN DAVAO DEL NORTE
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Zarate from PartyList Bayan Muna took the floor to bring to the attention of the Body some events that transpired the previous week which he believes government officials and employees, including the Members, could learn a lesson on how to conduct themselves with prudence, respect and courtesy in dealing with vulnerable sectors of society such as the indigenous peoples (IPs). He explained that the actuations of government officials and employees in question resulting to undue
governmental and official interference stemmed from their meeting last July 13 to 15, 2015 with the AtaManobo Lumads from Talaingod in Davao del Norte and San Fernando in Bukidnon who had sought sanctuary and refuge in the United Church of Christ in the Philippines in Haran, Davao City against the intensified military presence and operations in their communities. He adverted in particular to Rep. Nancy A. Catamco´s proposal to broker a dialogue between the tribal leaders of the Ata-Manobo and the representatives of the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP) to bring them back to their communities. He then narrated the events which led to the forcible
eviction of the Ata-Manobo from UCCP Haran
which resulted to violence, grave physical injuries, psychological trauma, and distress to the IPs. He maintained that Rep. Catamco´s actuations were clearly not becoming of a legislator, but were more of a law enforcer.
Apart from accomplishing the objectives of the
fact-finding mission that is to make a truthful assessment of the situation of the Ata-Manobo to come up with an appropriate response, Rep. Zarate emphasized the need for Congress to enact the appropriate policies that will protect the general welfare of the IPs as well as to address the main issues of the wrongful eviction of the Lumads, causes of the displacement of the lumads from their ancestral domains, militarization in
IP communities, violation of the constitutional and human rights, and the “misguided righteousness” of Rep. Catamco and government officials to compel the police to implement a rescue and forcible eviction of the lumads from their place of refuge and sanctuary. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.7,pp.30-31)

rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F093;
rows.title_full: HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS IN DAVAO CITY (HARAN INCIDENT)
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ilagan appealed for urgent and appropriate
action from Congress to address the plight of the indigenous peoples and their children. She adverted to the recent fact-finding mission on the situation of tribal schools, that she and Reps. Terry L. Ridon and Carlos Isagani T. Zarate as well as the Committee on Indigenous Cultural Communities and Indigenous Peoples Chairperson Nancy A. Catamco undertook in Cateel, Davao Oriental. Showing video presentations, she reported that the Armed Forces of the Philippines
(AFP) was using schools as barracks, destroying
property therein, and harassing students and
teachers accused of being members and supporters
of the New People´s Army; that hundreds of terrorized lumads subsequently sought sanctuary in the United Church of Christ of the Philippines (UCCP)in Haran, Davao City; and that Rep. Catamco insulted and berated the lumads during dialogues that ensued and illegally ordered local government forces as well as the police and military to forcibly bring them back to their lands. Rep. Ilagan then expressed support for the appeal
of the United Nations Special Rapporteur on the
Human Rights of Internally Displaced Persons for
the government to consult the indigenous peoples
and address the causes of their displacement; as well as the lumads´ call for peace and demilitarization of their communities. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.8,p.4)

rows.author: G105;
rows.title_full: WOMEN AND HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS (LUMAD'S PLIGHT)
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, upon motion of Rep.
Durano, Rep. Emmi A. De Jesus from Party-List
Gabriela spoke on how her own human rights have
been violated. She cited data on the number of cases of victims of extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances, mass killing of leaders and activists in different provinces and in Metro Manila, and the trumped-up charges against Party-List Members, including herself, under the regime of former President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo. She likewise expressed her disappointment on the continuing prevalence of such crimes on an even greater magnitude under the administration of President Benigno S. Aquino III particularly the cases of harassment and extrajudicial killings of the lumads in Talaingod, Province of Davao
del Norte by the 68th Infantry Battalion and the 4th Special Forces of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP). She maintained that as Party-List Representative of Gabriela, her participation to the cause of the AtaManobo was only limited to being part of the Save Our Schools (SOS) advocacy group to help the lumads resolve and make publicly known their internal displacement, repression, and human rights violations arising from intensified militarization, and unlawful arrest and intense and grave physical injuries and psychological trauma and distress from the forcible eviction by the Davao City Philippine National Police and the CIDG. Thereupon, Rep. De Jesus manifested her strong objection to the trumped-up and conspired charges filed by the CIDG against the Members of Congress and human rights advocates from the SOS and other support groups. She emphasized that the unlawful charges filed against them is a violation of their human rights which must be addressed as these are threats to freedom, civil liberties, and democracy. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.9,p.3)

rows.author: G022;
rows.title_full: SYSTEMATIC NEGLECT AND DISCRIMINATION OF THE LUMADS
rows.abstract:
Speaking in her capacity as Chairperson of the
Committee on Indigenous Cultural Communities and
Indigenous Peoples, Rep. Catamco brought to the attention of the Body the appeal of the leaders of the Ata Manobo and Matigsalung lumads based in Kapalong and Talaingod, Davao del Norte and San Fernando, Bukidnon for proper government interference and congressional action regarding the plight of the Lumad tribe whose people are being discriminated against and are being used by certain groups to rally against the present administration. She called on the Members to
come up with a legislative action that would strengthen the provisions of the Indigenous Peoples´ Rights Act (IPRA) on the protection of the rights of indigenous people, particularly with what is happening to the lumads in UCCP-Haran in Davao City. She underscored that the lumads were deceived into going to Davao with promises that they would be given sacks of rice and agricultural tools but nothing came out of it to the extent that most of the people who went to Haran became disappointed and depressed. Thereafter, an audio-visual presentation provided by an organization of lumads was made on the present condition of the lumads in Haran and how they are being treated like prisoners in spite of their plea to go
home to their respective families. Rep. Catamco then stated that the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) had already issued a report on what has been happening in Haran. After another audio-visual presentation showing her visit to Haran, she read some essential parts of the
DSWD report relating to the alleged deplorable living conditions of the lumads in the Haran compound. At this point, Rep. Catamco admonished those who were responsible for the lumads´ plight and who wanted to embarrass the PNoy Administration and poison the minds of her fellow tribe members about issues which they were not part of and did not understand. Airing videos and quoting from documents, she stressed that she did not usurp power during rescue operations; the lumads wanted the military, datus, and pertinent agencies to help them return to their lands
and did not really care about military presence as long as they were left to live in peace according to their customs and practices; and the view of the UN Special Rapporteur on the Human Rights for Internally Displaced Peoples was for the government to consult the lumads and ascertain their real views and feelings. She then said that the subject matter should be left to the
collective wisdom and conscience of the Chamber; and that the real and bigger problem which the government should address was the discrimination, abuse, and manipulation of the indigenous peoples.
Rep. Catamco stated that if the groups and organizations allegedly behind the lumads in Haran were really after the latter´s welfare, they should have instead advised the lumads to air their grievances to the concerned government agencies that are mandated to take proper actions on their complaints. She said that her Committee has consulted the different government agencies and would submit their recommendations on the matter. Stating that the issue of the lumads is not a question of personalities and parliamentary conduct, Rep. Catamco called on Congress, particularly the House Committees on Human Rights, Defense, and Indigenous Cultural Communities and Indigenous Peoples to thoroughly investigate the matter and ferret out the truth. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.10,p.13)

rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Acedillo, Ilagan and Zarate. Referred to the appropriate Committee. Manifestation by Rep. Atienza Re: Investigation re: Lumads

rows.author: F103;
rows.title_short: Budget In Preparation For The El Nino Phenomenon
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. Guanlao focused on the
proposed 2016 budget of the Department of
Agriculture (DA), the government´s failure to respond to calamities like the previous typhoons that ravaged the country´s agricultural sector, as well as its lack of preparedness to assist the farmers with the projected dry spell due to El Niño which is expected to decrease agricultural productivity. To address the problem, Rep. Guanlao
recommended that Congress, in scrutinizing the
proposed DA budget for 2016, should: 1) increase the Quick Response Fund (QRF) from the present P500 million to P2 billion for the repair and rehabilitation of irrigation canals and to use it to fund alternative plans to alleviate the devastating effects of El Niño; 2) cause
the release of the Agricultural Competitiveness
Enhancement Fund (ACEF) amounting to P7 billion to
support the farmers, use the ACEF to fund the
inclusion of farmers owning less than two hectares of land as beneficiaries of the Conditional Cash Transfer (CCT) Program or to provide them with alternative livelihood projects during nonplanting season, or use the Fund to strengthen the Philippine Crop Insurance Corporation (PCIC); 3) reprogram portions of the P32-billion allotment of the National Irrigation Administration (NIA) for the development of small water impounding projects, repair and rehabilitation of irrigation canals, and provision of water pumps and other water harvesting facilities for use of small
farmers. In conclusion, he said that the government should refocus the national budget and fiscal policy to the small farmers and other impoverished sectors of the rural communities needing priority government attention and support. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.15,p.5)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-09-01
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F056;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Robes took the floor to defend his name and
that of his family and Congress as an institution, and to stand on the side of truth, against the accusations being hurled against him by Atty. Levito Baligod, San Jose Del Monte City Mayor Reynaldo San Pedro and Ms. Bernadette Ricalde. He referred to newspaper reports published by the Philippine Daily Inquirer (PDI) from September 2 to September 5, 2015 where his name was included in the list of 20 Congressmen who were allegedly involved in a new P500-million pork barrel scam.
He lamented how through Atty. Baligod, he was
tried and convicted by publicity without being accorded the opportunity to defend himself. He thereafter gave the backgrounds of Messrs. Baligod and San Pedro as well as Ms. Ricalde and how they have allegedly connived to implicate him in the malversation of funds through falsification of documents, and of his wife´s alleged involvement in the killing of Ms. Ricalde´s husband. He then requested his colleagues to: 1) conduct an investigation in aid of legislation on the allegations of Ms. Ricalde and Atty. Baligod, particularly for the latter´s mishandling of the issue of the 20 solons whom he accused of graft; 2) craft laws that will govern the mechanisms and dynamics of whistle blowing; and 3) express the Members´ sentiments to the judicial branch to adopt administrative procedures that will improve the manner by which lawyers like Atty. Baligod handle accusations and/or allegations before ventilating the same in the media.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.17,p.3)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-09-07
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F100;
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. Colmenares spoke
about the high cost of electricity in the country, its impact on Filipino consumers and the nation´s economic development, and the need for the government to heed the demand for reduced prices of electricity. He underscored that the imposition of value-added tax (VAT) on electricity is the primary reason for its high cost, and proposed for its abolition to relieve the consumers from paying huge electric bills as well as to lower production costs and consequently, the prices of commodities. He likewise urged the Members to support and approve House Bill No. 344 and other related measures which seek the intervention of the government towards the abolition of VAT in the
price of electricity for the benefit of the Filipino people. INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Atienza discussed with Rep. Colmenares the reasons why the
government seems to be insensitive to the rising cost of electricity and the high price of gasoline and yet, it is against lowering the individual income tax rates; why the government does not explore the use of other sources of electricity like wind, water or coal-fired plants which it can tap to lower electricity costs; and whether the latter agrees with him that the PNoy Administration is insensitive to the needs and sentiments of the people. In closing, Rep. Atienza urged his colleagues to support the measure of Rep. Colmenares, seeking the abolition of VAT in the price of electricity. This and the proposal to remove the imposition of VAT on fuel products, could pave the way for the elimination of foreign influence in the Philippine economy.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.17,p.4)

rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep.Atienza. Referred to the Committe on Rules

rows.author: C072;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Lobregat recalled the painful and tragic
Zamboanga City siege that happened last September 9, 2013 which lasted for 21 days, when the elements of Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF)-Misuari forces attacked the City to raise the MNLF flag at the city´s seat of power. After the casualties and adverse effects of the Zamboanga siege, he stressed that the incident and the Cabatangan hostage-taking crisis which also took place in the City in 2001 showed the suffering of its people for becoming the collateral damage to the peace negotiations forged between the MNLF and the Philippine government. hope that such incident would not be repeated.

rows.author: H068;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Gutierrez from Akbayan Party-List expressed support for the indigenous peoples (IPs) of
Banaue who were faced with the challenge of stopping the construction of the Torre De Banaue Parking Building at the heart of their public plaza where communal activities, cultural events, and traditional festivities had been held for decades. As he raised the possible danger and hazards posed by the proposed parking project on the health and safety of the residents, the issue of the premature loan agreement entered into by the local government unit (LGU) of Ifugao, and the questionable ability of the contractor of the parking project, Rep. Gutierrez stated that the parking project is more about the environment,
culture and welfare of the community particularly on the use of the lands and resources of the IPs.
Given that the project would put the IPs´ rights and welfare at risk, Rep. Gutierrez urged his colleagues and the various government cultural and historical agencies such as the National Commission on the Indigenous Peoples (NCIP), the National Historical Commission of the Philippines (NHCP), and the National Commission for Culture and the Arts (NCCA) to stop the implementation of the parking project and help protect the IPs right to selfdetermination.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.21,p.4)

rows.author: H069;
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. Hicap spoke on the
evacuation of the Lumads from their community in
Surigao del Sur, citing in particular the extrajudicial killings of three Lumads by paramilitary groups and military soldiers. As he filed a Resolution calling for an investigation on the matter, he lamented that Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) Chief of Staff Hernando Iriberri and even the President had denied military involvement in said killings despite an ongoing militarization in the Lumad areas. He stated
that no one has been arrested or made accountable
even though there is an increasing number of
extrajudicial killings of Lumads under the PNoy
Administration. In closing, he enjoined his colleagues to protect and preserve the rights of the Lumads and the victims of Oplan Bayanihan in Mindanao. He also asked for the immediate consideration of House Resolutions No. 2358 and 1775, calling for the investigation of the
militarization of Mindanao, and the violation of rights of the Lumads. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.21,p.5)

rows.author: F048;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ong proposed that Congress call for a
constitutional convention to amend or draft a new
Constitution, and opined that the 1987 Constitution is obsolete, archaic and restrictive. He attributed poverty, graft and corruption, moral bankruptcy, increasing secessionist movement, opposition to the draft Basic Law on the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region, and possible failure by Congress to enact urgent and vital legislative measures to the ill-defined and shortsighted
provisions of the Constitution. He thereafter enumerated the following urgent constitutional issues that the convening body should tackle: 1) shift to parliamentary system of government;
2) parameters of investment policies; 3) refinement and delineation of election laws; 4) revamp of the Judiciary; and 5) creation of new and vital agencies to keep the country ahead of advances in science and technology, among others.
As he called on the Members to embrace the
challenge and assume responsibility for bringing order and decency in the country by removing monstrous provisions in the Constitution, he also appealed to them to approve the Resolution he authored calling for a constitutional convention to propose amendments to the 1987 Constitution.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Jose L. Atienza Jr.
focused on the description of the 1987 Constitution as “archaic,” and which Rep. Ong maintained is faulty because its provisions are obsolete and no longer fitted to address the needs of the present generation. The Members then discussed the constitutional provisions which Rep. Ong argued should be revised, including among others, the need to overhaul the judiciary system, shift to a parliamentary form of government, and adopt a unicameral legislature. Reps. Ong and Atienza agreed that the Constitution is defective.
Considering that this will be his last term in
Congress, Rep. Ong expressed his appreciation to the Members for allowing him to deliver his privilege speech. He then appealed to the chairperson of the Committee on Rules to schedule for discussion House Resolution No. 194, calling for the convening of a constitutional convention to amend the Constitution, which he filed and was officially received on August 13, 2013. Rep. Atienza suggested that Rep. Ong should file
a bill amending the Constitution instead of pursuing the adoption of his Resolution. He likewise urged the latter and the other Members of the House including the House leadership, to join him in crafting a measure calling for a constitutional convention to amend the defective provisions of the Constitution. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.21,p.5)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-09-15
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Atienza. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H058;
rows.abstract:
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Angelina
“Helen” D.L. Tan, M.D., from the Fourth District of Quezon informed the Body that during the historic meeting of the Asia Pacific Forum of the Global Tuberculosis Caucus held from August 31 to
September 1, 2015 in Sydney, Australia, the
parliamentarians from India, Vietnam, Indonesia,
Papua New Guinea, New Zealand and Australia have
given her the rare honor and grave responsibility of becoming the co-chair of the newly formed First Asia Tuberculosis Caucus. She said that this honor which she shared with the Honorable Warren Entsch of the Australian Parliament, was not only in recognition of her personal initiative to vigorously fight tuberculosis but the Chamber´s commitment to champion the cause of public health in the country. She then enumerated the goals of the Asia Pacific Caucus which included, among others, the aim to provide a strategic venue for
parliamentarians to work together across political and geographical divides; to promote bolder policies to stop tuberculosis; and to support patients and vulnerable groups and fight the stigma confronted by the patients and their families. Rep. Tan also discussed the efforts she has done to expedite the passage into law of House Bill No. 5042 and its Senate counterpart, establishing a comprehensive plan of action to eliminate tuberculosis as a public health problem.
She thereafter enjoined the Members´ support for
the enactment into law of House Bill No. 5042 and to be signatories to the Barcelona Declaration, an
initiative of the Global TB Caucus and which seeks the eradication of tuberculosis worldwide.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.21,pp.6-7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-09-15
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: H081;
rows.abstract:
Reiterating the issues that had been raised in the
halls of Congress regarding the Lumads staying in the United Church of Christ in the Philippines (UCCP) in Haran, Davao City, Rep. Zarate raised anew the alleged concerted effort by the military to subvert political freedom and human rights by allegedly filing criminal charges of illegal detention and child abuse against him and six others. He then explained to his colleagues why these charges are unfounded and baseless. In explaining further the personal consequences of
the trumped-up criminal charges against him, Rep.
Zarate emphasized that this kind of harassment and
intimidation is also happening to all progressive thinking individuals and activists serving the cause of the Lumads. He maintained that these trumped-up criminal charges that were also easily dismissed or discontinued by the courts for lack of evidence were elaborately initiated by the military to suppress, intimidate, and effect financial constraints against the accused.
Moreover, he claimed that the trumped-up
criminal charges against him by the military were filed to cover up its tracks on the rape of a 14-year old Lumad by a soldier during the raid in the UCCP-Haran and to deflect attention on the complaints against the military for its human rights violations in relation to its continued militarization of the indigenous communities in Davao del Norte. He opined that there is an ongoing war of attrition against the Lumads, and
that a state of impunity is wreaking havoc on the lives of the Lumads in Mindanao especially with the killings of some leaders and members of the Manobo Lumad tribe in Pangantucan, Bukidnon, and in San Miguel, Surigao del Sur, allegedly by special forces of the military. Rep. Zarate stressed that the Members are now being challenged to give their collective voice to condemn the invented cases filed against the Lumads and their supporters, as well as the widespread human rights violations being done against them. He thereafter emphasized the need to stop the killings of the Lumads and end the state of impunity that persists
throughout the country.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.21,p.7)

rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep. Bondoc,
Rep. Benhur L. Salimbangon from the Fourth
District of Cebu related how on September 12, 2015, a daylight robbery was committed against four female Chinese tourists on their way to Malapascua Island, Cebu Province. He said that all the resort operators in his district where the incident happened were so alarmed that he demanded from the Philippine National Police (PNP) Cebu Provincial Office headed by Superintendent Noel Gillamac the resolution of the case within 48 hours, and which the latter had accomplished on time. Given the speedy identification and arrest of the two perpetrators, he read before the Body the House Resolution that he authored commending
Supt. Gillamac and his men and enjoined his
colleagues to approve the same. Rep. Salimbangon also moved that all Members from Cebu City and Cebu Province be made coauthors of the said resolution. INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Reps. Atienza and Salimbangon then discussed
the reasons for the crimes committed against the tourists and its discouraging effects to the tourism industry. Rep. Atienza also urged Tourism Secretary Ramon Jimenez to do something about the peace and order condition in the country´s tourist spots for the benefit of the tourism industry. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.22,pp.1-2)

Rep. Colmenares noted the high income taxes
imposed on taxpayers in the country; and the lack of government reform in the taxation system from 1987 to 2015 which causes injustice on all taxpayers. Continuing with his speech upon Rep. Bondoc´s motion, Rep. Colmenares pointed out that in a study conducted by Bayan Muna Party-List, the taxpayers would have not been burdened with high income taxes if only the government had reformed its taxation scheme. rows.author: H065;
rows.abstract:
As the country commemorates the declaration of
martial law on September 21, 1972, Rep. Atienza
called on all levels of government officials to remember the lessons thereof and not to abuse their newfound freedom and authority. He focused in particular on the government of Manila City, how it has been depriving its people, especially the poor, of their rights to free health centers, playgrounds and swimming pools, and most of all, the use of public markets. He expressed apprehension that the privatization of public markets in Manila might encourage other local
governments throughout the country to sell their
markets because they are located in prime real estate and would fetch huge amounts of money. He then called on the public market vendors to fight for their rights against privatization. In closing, he remarked that the lessons from the
past should not be forgotten but in unity, the people must overcome the challenges of the present times with God´s help.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BAGATSING
Before his interpellation, Rep. Bagatsing congratulated Rep. Atienza for voicing out the sentiments of the people of Manila over the privatization of their public markets. Rep. Atienza then recalled the improvements made to the public markets without resorting to privatization during his term as mayor of Manila. Reps. Atienza and Bagatsing then discussed the compelling reasons for the privatization of the public
markets without public consultation or hearing; the questionable awarding of contract to a nonexistent office to the detriment of the market stallholders; and the City Hall of Manila´s violation of the Procurement Law.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
Recognized by the Chair, Reps. Jonathan A. Dela
Cruz and Atienza discussed the laws and provisions
governing the operation and maintenance of public
markets and the protection of vendors and consumers; the essence of the operation of public markets vis-Ã -vis public service; the number of market vendors and small entrepreneurs affected by the privatization of public markets in Manila; the latter´s opinion regarding the modernization program and not privatization of public markets; and the creation of cooperatives in response to the modernization of public markets. Rep. Atienza also proposed that local government units (LGUs) should provide the essential service of operating clean, wholesome and effectively managed public markets; and that original stallholders and vendors should be prioritized once a public market is modernized. He thereafter explained the effects of privatizing public markets in Manila on the ownership of market stalls under the so-called “first-preference option,” on the ordinary housewives who buy their food supply from the public market, and on public transportation
in view of market vendors relocated along the
road. He maintained that the privatization of a public market negates its role as an essential public service to benefit the community. Rep. Dela Cruz concurred with Rep. Atienza´s argument
and added that small traders and poor Filipinos
would be the most affected by the privatization. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.23,pp.10-11)

... Rep. Carlos Isagani T. Zarate of Bayan Muna Party-List rose to denounce the six-year old Maguindanao massacre and other instances of extrajudicial killings committed by warlords, private armies, paramilitary groups, and agents in other parts of the country; and to ask for justice for the victims thereof. He criticized the current administration for reneging on its promise to revoke Executive Order (EO) No. 546 which paramilitary groups had used to justify their
atrocities; for failing to solve hundreds of cases of killings of journalists, environmentalists, indigenous peoples, and members of marginalized sectors; and for allowing the reign of impunity to continue especially in mining areas and big plantations because it needed the warlords for its political interests. He then demanded that the government disarm and disband said groups, speedily resolve the aforecited cases, and revoke the pertinent EO. INTERPELLATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
To Rep. Dela Cruz´ request for data on killings
similar to the Maguindanao Massacre, Rep. Zarate
reiterated the facts and figures on extrajudicial killings and human rights violations including those that had recently happened in South Cotabato and Surigao del Sur. After a discussion on the rising tide of criminality and proliferation of paramilitary groups and private armies in the country, both Reps. Zarate and Dela Cruz urged Congress to investigate the killings perpetrated by paramilitary groups and to look into the revocation of EO No. 546 which became the basis
for said proliferation.

rows.author: H064;
rows.abstract:
At the outset, Rep. Alejano conveyed, on behalf
of Magdalo Para sa Pilipino Party-List, their profound sympathy and heartfelt condolences to the victims of the terror attacks in Paris, France. Offering a moment of silence to the victims, he then spoke on the monstrosities of terrorism and pointed out that each and every nation should take security issues seriously as no country is beyond the reach of terror organizations such as the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria (ISIS) which had claimed responsibility for the terror attacks not only in Paris but all over the world. Citing several past and present acts of terrorism in the country including the 2007 Batasan bombing, Rep. Alejano stated that the Philippines is also a hot
spot for violent extremism. He then called on the
government to immediately formulate a national security strategy that will guide the Filipino nation towards advancing and protecting its national interests and urged Congress to look into the implementation of Republic Act No. 9372 or the Human Security Act considering that it has remained toothless in combating terrorism and useless in prosecuting terrorists. He said that he filed a resolution seeking to inquire on the status and implementation of the Human Security Act and urged the House to revitalize the Joint Oversight Committee on Human Security Act. In closing, he enjoined his colleagues to advocate
for the strengthening of the country´s national security.
(Source: House Journal No.32,pp.6&7)

rows.abstract:

This, in spite of the high security risks and threats caused by the recent Paris attacks.
Similarly, Rep. Bataoil commended the various

one-government approach to facilitate the success of the APEC-ELM. He expressed hope that government

As shown in the 2015 APEC meeting, he stated that the Philippines has been able to showcase to the world that it can be a real republic, and a center of economic development and cooperation in the region.

rows.author: B006;
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, upon motion of Rep.
Romualdo, Deputy Speaker Balindong rose on a
question of personal and collective privilege and
pleaded for the cause of peace. He asked the administration as well as Congress to work for the enactment of the Bangsamoro Basic Law (BBL) as he observed their silence, inaction, and lack of concern thereon for the past several months. As he thanked the peace efforts of all sectors and stakeholders, he stressed that the Muslims and indigenous peoples of Mindanao have been waiting for their right to selfdetermination for centuries; governance is the key to uplifting the socioeconomic wellbeing of Muslim Mindanao; and that the draft BBL, which has undergone so much investment and consultation nationwide, is the proper vehicle to identify and address its needs. He also cited facts and figures on the billions
of pesos that the public and business sectors have lost and on the lives that have been wasted and displaced, due to the war in Mindanao. Deputy Speaker Balindong, in his quest for lasting
peace in Mindanao, then enjoined his colleagues
to work earnestly toward the passage of the BBL considering that the measure has been scheduled for plenary discussions since June. He stated that there are concerns and issues that need to be resolved and that it is imperative for the Members to find a solution to the Mindanao conflict and bring genuine and lasting peace and development in Mindanao. MANIFESTATION OF MINORITY LEADER ZAMORA (R.) As he joined the call of Rep. Balindong for Congress to put an end to the deliberations on the draft BBL and for the Members to review the individual provisions of the said measure, Rep. Zamora suggested that the House leadership should call for an all party caucus to discuss the many issues that have been raised, such as the opt-in provision in the BBL and work out something that is within the ambit of the Constitution and is acceptable not only to one community or a particular group but to the entire Filipino
people. He explained that even though he represents a highly urbanized city far from Mindanao, it is his duty to do something to help resolve the Mindanao conflict. 
(House Journal No.35, p.3)

rows.author: F100;
rows.abstract: Rep. Colmenares acknowledged the camaraderie, support and respect of his colleagues and the House leadership despite their having had differences on certain issues; and said that he wanted to reiterate his maiden speech on human rights in order to remind them of the vagaries of martial law. He then recounted in detail the torture he suffered at the hands of police and military forces at the time, who alleged that he was a member of the New People´s Army although he was merely a student leader of the Student Catholic Action. He stressed that although he survived, he would never forget the torture he experienced as well as the idea that a person can commit such form of heinous crimes merely for the fun of exercising power over another person´s life. He stated that the martial law period remains a bloody chapter in the country´s history and that he could attest to the fact that torture was committed not only to him but to many of his codetainees as well. He expressed hope that martial law would never be repeated. INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA After being clarified that Rep. Colmenares was arrested without given the chance to exercise his rights as a Filipino citizen and thereafter subjected to severe torture by military authorities, Rep. Atienza said that this experience should serve as a reminder to all the Members about the incidents during the dark years of martial law, and not allow the same mistakes to happen again. He stressed that Congress should guide the youth on the right path to democracy. This, as he lamented that the human rights violators were not meted out any punishment. He said that he was glad that the period of martial law can now be openly and truthfully discussed by the people, and underscored that this should never be imposed again because dictatorship and tyrannical rule would never lead to prosperity and economic emancipation. Rep. Atienza opined that the actions of a politician who promises to impose a one-man rule and commits acts of violence are never justifiable. He then encouraged Rep. Colmenares to continue telling his story and expressed hope that Rep. Colmenares will win as a senator so he can continue to inspire the people, defend human rights, and promote the ideals of democracy. (SOURCE: House Journal No.40,p.1)

rows.author: A016;
rows.title_short: Peace And Order Situation In Zamboanga Sibugay
rows.abstract:
Upon recognition of the Chair, Rep. Cabilao recalled the uncoordinated December 8, 2015 raid conducted by members of the Zamboanga Sibugay Mobile Force and the 44th Infantry Battalion in Talusan, Zamboanga Sibugay which left three people dead, including three-term Talusan Councilor Basilisa Llanos who was shot three times on the head inside her room, and a pregnant woman. She read into the record the report of the Commission on Human Rights (CHR) on the incident as published in ABS-CBN Online News, highlighting the failure of the raiding police team to identify themselves and to consider the civilian population surrounding the target area.  She then urged her colleagues to conduct an independent and immediate investigation of the incident for the sake of the residents of Olutanga Island, to prevent the death of more people, and not for any similar incident to happen in Talusan´s adjacent municipalities.

rows.author: B006;
rows.title_short: Passage Of Basic Law On Bangsamoro Autonomous Region
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Defensor, the Chair recognized
Deputy Speaker Pangalian M. Balindong who
expressed hope for the successful enactment of the
draft Bangsamoro Basic Law (BBL) during the 16th
Congress, and uttered gratitude for the fruitful House party caucus with the President on the BBL. He denied allegations that bribery was used as a strategy for the approval of the BBL, emphasizing that the resumption of its deliberations was a product of both goodwill and renewed realization that peace is necessary and nonnegotiable. He implored his Muslim and Christian brothers and sisters, especially his colleagues in the House to renew and reinvigorate the hope for a final and lasting solution for peace. The Deputy Speaker expressed confidence that the Members would be able to pass the Basic Law for the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region (BLBAR) next year considering that they have gained a new momentum with the continued deliberations thereon. He then advised the Members to use their collective power to provide the institutional means and structures
to strengthen and affirm their respective heritage
and identities. In closing his speech, he expressed belief that the best and the only solution to the Mindanao conflict is peace and therefore, it is their responsibility and a
legacy of the 16th Congress to make every effort possible to seize this historic opportunity to provide a lasting peace in the Mindanao region and the entire country. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.41,p.12)

rows.author: F100;
rows.title_short: Veto Of S S S Bill
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, on motion of Rep. Banal,
Rep. Neri J. Colmenares took issue on the veto by
President Benigno S. Aquino III of the measure
providing for the increase in the monthly pension of Social Security System (SSS) pensioners. He
maintained that the President´s veto was on the
premise that the SSS, on the basis of actuarial studies, will turn bankrupt if the present monthly pension of SSS pensioners amounting to P1,200 would be increased by P2,000 as proposed in the measure. He subsequently explained the following issues that President Aquino had disregarded in justifying his veto: that the Philippine government is the sole guarantor of the SSS funds and its solvency; and the existence of a source of fund for the P2,000-increase in monthly pension. He further said that the SSS can have additional sources of funds if it will only improve its collections, cut down its operational expenses,
perks, bonuses, and retirement benefits of its board members, and request for government subsidy. He further discussed the positive impact of increasing the monthly pension of SSS pensioners to the national economy. Rep. Colmenares then stressed that the real issue was that the current pension was inadequate amidst inflation. As he relayed the anger of pensioners over the President´s veto, he expressed hope that the next
administration would be more efficient and
responsive. Adding that the President should respect the will of the House and the Senate which passed the Bill twice, he enjoined his colleagues to historically override the veto.
(Source: House Journal No.48,p.9)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2016-01-27
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: B006;
rows.title_short: Failure To Pass The B B L Bill
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Belmonte (J.), the Chair next
recognized Deputy Speaker Pangalian M. Balindong
who rued the fact that the Bangsamoro Basic Law
would not be passed thereby consequently foreclosing all possible peaceful, legal and constitutional avenues for peace. He stressed that the measure offered the Muslims the recognition of their identity, an opportunity for self-determination, and a guarantee of
equality with non-Muslims; but that because of the
Mamasapano encounter, they became labelled as
terrorists and traitors. He pointed out that the Chamber failed to fulfill its commitment to the Bangsamoro people, the expectations of the international community, and the legacy of the President. Nevertheless, he opined that the minority in the country might have lost in terms of numbers but never in the discourse as it sprang from the justness and legitimacy of its cause.

rows.author: G057;
rows.title_short: Bangsamoro Basic Law ( B B L )
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Tupay T. Loong
expressed his sentiment on the failure of the Body to pass the proposed Bangsamoro Basic Law which, he said, might have been adversely affected by the
Mamasapano incident last January 25, 2015. He
expressed belief that the inability of the Body to pass the BBL is a failure on their part to provide the legislative support necessary to finally end the Bangsamoro secessionist movement and bring peace and unity to the country. He then hoped that the next Congress will be more understanding and
compassionate when it takes up the BBL again.
Thereafter, in behalf of his constituents, Rep.
Loong expressed his gratitude to the following with regard to the BBL: 1) President Benigno S. Aquino III, for his sincere effort to solve the Bangsamoro problem and give the people the just peace they deserve; 2)Speaker Feliciano Belmonte Jr. for his unwavering support for the passage of the BBL; 3)Rep. Rufus B. Rodriguez for competently handling the difficult task of chairing the Ad Hoc Committee on the Bangsamoro Basic Law; 4)the Members who participated in the deliberation to make the BBL constitutional, just, and acceptable to the Filipinos; 5)the peace-loving people from different geographical areas here and abroad; 6) the various sectors of society who strongly supported the passage of the BBL; and 7)the international community such as the
International Contact Group which included the
United Kingdom, Turkey, Japan, and the Kingdom of
Saudi Arabia that provided advice and assistance in order to reach landmark agreements. Then thanking his constituents for their support,
Rep. Loong promised to pursue the passage of the BBL in the 17th Congress if elected for another term and continue the parliamentary struggle for justice and peace. He agreed that the Bangsamoro problem was not a constitutional but a political problem and should be solved politically and not through violence. However, he said that he could not blame the Bangsamoro people if they took the path of war in order to preserve and protect their identity, religion, and ancestral land. (Source: House Journal No.49, pp.6-7)

rows.author: G086;

rows.abstract:
Rep. Sema initially pointed out that the 1987

rows.author: H034;
rows.title_short: House Bill No.6328 Exoanded Protected Areas N I P A S
rows.abstract:
Rep. Hagedorn took the floor to condemn the
unethical behavior of a few Members regarding the
discussions on House Bill No. 6328, expanding the
National Integrated Protected Areas System (NIPAS)
Act of 1992. He informed the Body of the alleged
controversial Committee deliberations on the measure wherein no public consultations were conducted, provisions were being deleted by the Committee secretariat without proper consultations, and prominent environmentalists and other concerned sectors expressed their objection to the exclusion of Palawan from the coverage of said measure. After filing a formal protest, Rep. Hagedorn stated that the Committee on Rules recommitted House Bill No. 6328 and the Committee on Natural Resources decided to restore the five protected areas in Palawan. He lamented however that during the deliberations the previous week, Reps. Jonathan A. Dela Cruz and Mark A. Villar attempted to delete the provisions regarding the protected areas in Palawan. He thereafter expressed his desire to get written and formal answers from Reps. Villar and Dela Cruz as the Sponsor and presentor of the measure, and asked
whether the latter did not lie when he declared that there were no Committee amendments, despite
knowledge of the fact that an executive meeting was called to correct the anomaly that attended the deletion of the provision on the five protected areas. He asked whether a new amendment calling for said deletion is tantamount to an amendment to the sponsoring Committee´s decision and report. Furthermore, he inquired into Rep. Villar´s motive in proposing for the removal of Palawan´s four protected areas, this as he stressed that the people therein know what is best for the future of their province. Finally, he relayed the sentiments of his people as to why some Members have become callous and insensitive because of their desire for power. The Chair noted the statements made by Rep.Hagedorn.
REMARKS OF MAJORITY LEADER GONZALES
To set the record straight and to address the
insinuation that something unethical was made during the session of January 27, 2016, Majority Leader Gonzales clarified that the parliamentary status of the said Bill was that it was still in the period of amendments, with no individual nor Committee amendments taken on the floor by the sponsoring Committee. He stressed that the Rules of the House provide that a Member may propose his amendments during the period of amendments and it is therefore incumbent upon him to be present in the Session Hall to ensure that his proposal would be taken up on the floor. Thus, he emphasized that the Bill has not undergone any illegal nor unethical process as it is still in the period of amendments, nor was there any violation of the Rules insofar as it is concerned. The Chair noted the statement of the Majority Leader.(Source: House Journal No.49,p.27)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2016-02-01)

rows.author: C009;
rows.abstract:
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Albano cited
in his speech the perennial problem of massive
flooding in Metro Manila and in the provinces
brought about by heavy rains and typhoons that frequently hit the country. Specifically, he spoke on the following issues: the government´s mitigation measures and master plan to address the massive flooding and the substantial budgetary allocation given to government agencies relative to these issues. He thereafter inquired into the status of the government´s flood control programs and asked how the different departments/agencies and local government units (LGUs) coordinate with each other to address the said problem. He thereafter enjoined both Houses of Congress to pass a resolution urging the proper committees to conduct an investigation in aid of legislation into the state of implementation of the master plans for flood control and mitigation, the
construction and rehabilitation of flood  structures along priority river basins, and the persistent flooding in the Philippines. He called on the next President to appoint again Secretary Rogelio Singson as water czar and as Secretary of the DPWH to continue what he has started.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
In his interpellation, Rep. Atienza called on
DPWH Secretary Singson to address the problem of
flooding because the country will never prosper economically unless the flooding situation is solved. While Rep. Albano believed that Secretary Singson is not remiss in his duties, Rep. Atienza opined that Secretary Singson should step down from his position considering that many projects are being left unattended including the two big flood control projects in Mandaluyong and Manila.
INTERPELLATION OF DEPUTY SPEAKER APOSTOL
Recognized by the Chair, Deputy Speaker Sergio
A. F. Apostol inquired whether Rep. Albano´s statistics included the provinces of Leyte and Samar to which the latter replied that he did not have the data regarding the two provinces. (House Journal No.50,pp.10-11)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2016-02-02
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Atienza

rows.author: G105;
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Emmi A. De
Jesus delved into certain issues confronting women
and children particularly on how they should have a place in the electoral campaign which was set to start on February 9. Since March 8 is considered the International Women´s Day and the month of March as International Month for Women, Rep. De Jesus informed her colleagues that Gabriela Women´s Party is not forfeiting the observance of the month dedicated for women. She believed that the election season is an opportune moment to bring women´s issues into the forefront of election debates to better inform the electorate and help them make better decisions. Rep. De Jesus explained that the Gabriela Women´s Party will make the election campaign period as the public tribunal for trying perpetrators of such abuses and discussing public policies that cause unemployment and poverty, inadequate social services, unemployment, and human rights violations including recent incidents of extrajudicial killings among lumads. She said that as part of its “Labanan ang Abuso” theme, the Makabayan bloc will continue to advocate propeople, prowomen, propoor laws, policies,
and services; peace talks with the National
Democratic Front and release of political prisoners; cessation of extrajudicial killings and other human rights violations; respect for ancestral domain; and the breakup of paramilitary groups and return of military forces to the barracks. Thereupon, Rep. De Jesus challenged her
colleagues to make the campaign more meaningful by
discussing the aforementioned issues.(Source: House Journal No.50,p.11)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2016-02-02

rows.author: H081;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Zarate initially said that the Makabayan
block recognized the Bangsamoro struggle for national self-determination and the Filipino people´s oppression and exploitation by colonial and neocolonial powers and the local political and business elite. He then explained how the draft Basic Law for the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region (BLBAR) did not grant full autonomy to the Bangsamoro region by limiting its powers such as on the full use and exploitation of mineral and energy resources and on the amendment or invalidation of the Mining Act, Electric
Power Industry Reform Act (EPIRA), and other
exploitative and oppressive laws. He elucidated on
how autonomy can never be possible under a neocolonial, semifeudal, corrupt, and exploitative state and ruling system. He stressed that the measure did not address the social and economic roots of poverty and injustice. He concluded that because of all of this, the Bangsamoro people´s armed struggle will continue and might even intensify. Even if Congress had failed to pass a meaningful law, Rep. Zarate stated that the Makabayan bloc would continue to support measures that would strengthen the right to self-determination of the Moro people, as well as the lumads. He added that the socioeconomic roots of war must be identified and dismantled and that programs for genuine land reform, job creation, industrialization and wealth redistribution
should be instituted. (Source: House Journal No.50, pp.11-12)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2016-02-02

rows.author: H069;
rows.abstract:
In commemoration of the Mendiola and Lupao
massacres, Rep. Hicap spoke in Filipino on the lack of genuine land reform programs of the government. He stated that years have passed and many Administrations had promised land reform programs, including the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program (CARP), but the farmers are still praying to till a land of their own. He said that in their fight for genuine land reform, the farmers are instead being neglected and massacred as shown by the Mendiola and Lupao massacres, the extrajudicial killings of farmers, the land conversion projects, and the blatant disregard of the Aquino government for the farmer beneficiaries
in Hacienda Luisita. Finally, Rep. Hicap stressed his Party-List´s call for the immediate approval of the Genuine Agrarian Reform Bill which aims to give free lands to the farmers and ensure the protection of their rights, and for justice to be served to the victims of the Mendiola and Lupao massacres. (House Journal No.50,p.12)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2016-02-02

rows.author: G003;
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep. Banal,
Rep. Emmeline Aglipay-Villar asked the House
to use its power of oversight to safeguard the rights of children, and cited five laws aimed at protecting their rights and welfare. She however noted that based on the study made by the Philippine Legislators´ Committee on Population and Development to which she belongs, certain problems have been encountered for the full implementation of the mandates of Republic Act ( RA) No. 7610 or the Special Protection of Children Against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act, RA No. 9208 or the Anti-
Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003, RA No. 9262 or
the Anti-Violence Against Women and their Children
Act of 2004, RA No. 9344 or the Juvenile Justice and Welfare Act of 2006, and RA No. 9775 or the Anti-Child Pornography Act of 2009. This, she reasoned, was due to the 1) people´s lack of full awareness about these laws, 2) improper and incorrect handling by the government agencies concerned, 3) lack of clarity in the manner and procedure of handling juvenile delinquents, 4) courts´ attitude of not being “child-friendly,” 5) failure of victims to pursue their case, and 6) confusion in inter-agency cooperation and partnership. As she stressed the need for the House to look into the implementation of laws through legislative inquiry and for the Committee on Welfare of Children to exercise its oversight functions, Rep. Aglipay-Villar also emphasized the need to review the situation of LGUs with respect to law enforcement, and for the House to find proper avenues to make the laws truly protective of children (SOURCE: House Journal No.50,p.12)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2016-02-02

rows.author: H041;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Leonardia took the floor to recount the
tragedy that befell the Uy family of Bacolod City
during the 2013 Christmas holiday because of lack of security at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Terminal 3. He related that the casualties were the young boy who died on the spot, his equally young cousin whose head was pierced by a bullet and who to this day still bears the hole therein, and their two elders who are both still suffering from physical and emotional injuries. He lamented that both the airport management and the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) as the insurer of the airport have refused to take responsibility and pay any liabilities for the incident. He thereafter called for a review of the
security measures in the airports and other terminals; the division of responsibilities among the security forces that operate therein; and the GSIS insurance coverage in the areas. He also asked the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) to look into the case of the Uy family. (SOURCE: House Journal No.50,pp.12-13)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2016-02-02

rows.author: C072;
rows.title_short: Passage Or Non-passage Of Bangsamoro Basic Law
rows.abstract:
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Celso L.
Lobregat from the First District of Zamboanga City
spoke on the following reasons for the passage or
nonpassage of the Bangsamoro Basic Law (BBL) in
the House of Representatives: 1) the abolition of the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (ARMM)
and the repeal of RA No. 9054; 2) the deletion of 14 provisions of the BBL Bill because of constitutionality, conflict with existing law and the issue on powers of government; 3) the position of the MILF that the passage of Congress of the agreed BBL draft should have no changes and should not diminish, dilute or water down its provisions except for a minor one that will enhance or improve it; and 4) the violation of the President´s instruction to the government peace
panel that the law must be mindful of the Constitution including its flexibilities, learn from the lessons of the past, exclude provisions that cannot be delivered economically, socially, and politically during his term, and consultative and be transparent. Aside from the many unconstitutional provisions and contentious and controversial provisions inimical to the national interest and sovereignty of the State, Rep. Lobregat also pointed out the other factors that
had caused the delay in the passage of the Bill.
He also stated that if ever Congress should pass
the BBL in the future, the Members should not only
properly observe the legislative process but more importantly, pass a law that can stand legal and constitutional scrutiny, is not against the national interest or the interest of the people of Mindanao and Zamboanga City, does not contain provisions inimical to the territorial integrity and sovereignty of the Republic, and does not have provisions leading to the creation of a substate.
MANIFESTATION OF REP. LOBREGAT
Rep. Lobregat recalled that he was in the final
stage of delivering his speech en contra on House
Bill No. 5811 or the proposed BLBAR. Considering
the time constraints, he then requested that the remainder of his said speech be inserted into the Record of the House.. . .INSERTION INTO THE RECORD
OF REP. LOBREGAT´S SPEECH EN CONTRA On further motion of Rep. Alvarez (F.), there being no objection, the Body approved to insert into the
Record the speech en contra of Rep. Lobregat on
House Bill No. 5811 or the draft BLBAR. (SOURCE: House Journal No.50,p.13)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2016-02-02

rows.author: H075;
rows.title_short: Basic Law For The Bangsamoro Autonomous Region (blbar)
rows.abstract:
Rep. Turabin-Hataman stressed that after all has
been said and done about the proposed Basic Law for the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region (BLBAR), she
would like her colleagues to bear with their frustrations and hurt because while it may not be their sole chance to attain peace, the Bill could have been the door that they have long waited for and labored to be opened. As she was no longer inclined to answer the accusations that have been hurled against them, like the Mamasapano massacre and the allegations that the Moro people are violent and not trustworthy, with the provisions of the measure suspected as being geared towards something else, she asked why Congress should decide on the fate and lives of people based on its own ignorance, and underscored that those who walk with humility and confronted by an ignorant person should say “peace and move away.” (SOURCE: House Journal No.51,p.15)

rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F100;
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Colmenares
spoke about the bill increasing by P2,000 the pension of Social Security System (SSS) members, which both Houses of Congress had deliberated on since 2011 and subsequently approved into law only to be vetoed by President Benigno S. Aquino III on January 12, 2016 on the ground that it would bankrupt the SSS. Rep. Colmenares averred that just like in other countries, the Philippine government should subsidize SSS if there is a need for additional pension funds. As regards studies on bankruptcy being done by the SSS every four years, Rep. Colmenares pointed out that no SSS in the whole world goes bankrupt precisely because actuarial studies are merely studies to know up to when the funds would last, thus measures are made to avoid bankruptcy. Thereafter, wanting to leave behind a legacy in the 16th Congress, Rep. Colmenares stated that he would be very thankful if the House leadership would be able to muster enough Members to override the veto of President
Aquino. MOTION OF REP. LAGDAMEO (M.)
REMARKS OF REP. ATIENZA
At this point, saying that he is one with Rep.
Colmenares´ stand on the additional P2,000 for SSS
pensioners, Rep. Jose L. Atienza Jr. asked that the Body should do something right this time in order to correct what they have been doing improperly for the past three years. (House Journal No.52,p.4)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2016-05-23

rows.author: H094;
rows.title_short: First And Final Address To Congress
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Ty-Delgado
talked about her belief in Philippine democracy, and that there are still men and women whose humanity transcend their self-interest, whose lives are ruled by what is right, and whose hearts are a lot bigger than the power they hold.
Thereafter, Rep. Ty-Delgado gave a backgrounder
of her public service as vice mayor and mayor of
Tandag, Surigao del Sur, and her tough journey to a congressional seat. Believing that a congressional office is a platform for real change in governance, she said that this is what made her go on a steadfast pursuit for said seat. Rep. Ty-Delgado then called on those who will be coming back in the next Congress to work together with the incoming administration of President-elect
Rodrigo R. Duterte. Subsequently telling
her colleagues that the nearing end of their terms
should not stop them from building a united nation, she urged them to share their lives with the unfortunate. (Source: House Journal No.52,p.35)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2016-05-23)
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

its mandate to canvass the votes for President and
Vice-President in the 2016 elections, in a recordsetting three days. He asked his colleagues to thank and recognize the Speaker and urged them to continue the institution´s legislative legacy. (SOURCE: House Journal No.52,p.78)
